name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention. Domain anim/walk; descriptor step_down accurately reflects the body: a 6-frame animated walk step that moves runtime_char[char_idx] +1 in Y (south), sets facing byte = 0 (south), optionally scrolls the viewport down, and ends one tile lower. No Ghidra address residue in the name. Caller fd2_walk_path_animation_loop dispatches direction byte 0 -> this function, confirming 'down' semantics.
purpose: Animate one south (+1 y) walk step for runtime_char[char_idx]: set facing south, play a 6-frame slide (scrolling the battle viewport down when the character is past the lower window margin and the window is not yet at the map bottom edge), advance the character's tile/world position, then fire tile-step events.
logic_summary: 1) Cache pos_y (pChar[1]); set facing byte (pChar[3]) = 0 (south); clear walk_anim_y_scroll_rows; init blit_offset = 0x8088. 2) Scroll decision: if (pos_y - view_window_origin_y) <= 5 OR window already at bottom edge (map_height_tiles - view_window_max_y == view_window_origin_y), then just bump cursor_screen_y (no scroll: scroll_delta_y=0, scroll_window_flag=0); else set scroll_delta_y=0x720 and scroll_window_flag=1. 3) 6-frame loop (frame 1..6): tick tutorial-progress SFX, palette-cycle anim, set walk_anim_phase (pChar[4]) = frame, tick chapter palette anim; accumulate compose_walk_step_y_sub_pixel_offset += scroll_delta_y and walk_anim_y_scroll_rows += scroll_window_flag; composite battle tile-map (height 8 when not scrolling, 9 when scrolling) from large_game_state_buffer+0x8088; composite all char overlays; advance blit_offset by scroll_delta_y; blit the assembled frame to VGA (0xA0504) from large_game_state_buffer+blit_offset; wait one BIOS tick. 4) Finalize: pos_y++ (pChar[1]); view_window_origin_y += scroll_window_flag (commit scroll); cursor_world_y++; reset walk_anim_phase (pChar[4]) = 0; clear compose_walk_step_y_sub_pixel_offset and walk_anim_y_scroll_rows. 5) Call fd2_check_tile_event_post_action(cursor_world_x, cursor_world_y, 0) to trigger any tile-step event at the new position.

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Index into the battle runtime_char array (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr); selects which character takes the south walk step. Body uses it as runtime_char_array_ptr[char_idx] (stride RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE=0x50) for the pos/facing/anim-phase byte writes, and forwards it to fd2_tick_tutorial_progress_with_sfx.
params.reason: Live Ghidra name param_1 is a generic placeholder; the value is the runtime_char array index. src/ already names it char_idx, which matches every sibling walk-step function (left/up/right) and the array-index usage. Rename to be applied in Stage 2.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects only: mutates runtime_char[char_idx] position/facing/anim-phase bytes, advances cursor/view-window globals, drives the frame animation, and triggers tile-step events at the destination.

notes: Comment block (aniwalk.c lines 54-60) already accurate and concise (6-frame walk step DOWN +1y, facing=0 south, viewport scroll, shared epilogue calling fd2_check_tile_event_post_action); kept verbatim, no src edit. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with refined understanding; not modified. Field-offset note: this engine's runtime_char base pointer points at the position fields, so src byte offsets pChar[0]=pos_x, pChar[1]=pos_y, pChar[3]=facing, pChar[4]=walk_anim_phase are equivalent to the Ghidra struct fields bPos_y / pSprite_state[1] / pSprite_state[2] (verified against RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE=0x50 and KB runtime_char layout 0x08 coords / 0x0A graphic-direction-run); not a logic discrepancy. Scroll condition '< 6' (decomp/plate) vs '<= 5' (src) are identical for signed ints; equivalent. Single caller: fd2_walk_path_animation_loop @ 0x13488 (dispatch byte 0 = down).
